chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban from Amr ibn Khalid from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah! We do not enter a house wherein is a picture of a human being, nor a house wherein it is urinated in, nor a house wherein is a dog.'

key_terms.يُبَالُ فِيهِ: Where urination takes place (place of excretion)

ai.seo_question: Why do angels not enter houses with pictures or dogs?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the triad of impediments to angelic entry—images, urine, and dogs—emphasizing the physical and spiritual cleanliness required for divine presence. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the concept of *Taharah* (purity) as a prerequisite for *Tajalli* (manifestation) of the angels, reinforcing the domestic sphere as a microcosm of worship. The inclusion of 'images' (*suwar*) specifically points to the broader theological concern with idolatry and visual distraction in the believer's home.
